subject: Data deletion workflow & backup constraints — follow-up from discovery call
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@brightfin.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 May 2026 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Data deletion workflow & backup constraints — follow-up from discovery call

Hi Lena — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. I summarized what I heard on the call and flagged open questions for our infra/legal teams.

Summary of BrightFin requirements (as discussed):
- PII scope: user profile fields (name, email, phone), payment identifiers (tokenized), and AI-derived embeddings tied to user IDs.
- Right-to-be-forgotten (RTBF): requests can be initiated via API or support portal; BrightFin requires proof-of-deletion confirmation once completed.
- Retention: business-critical logs OK, but BrightFin policy requires "no residual personal data in restored backups beyond 30 days" where regulative scope applies.
- Logging/Observability: audit logs for deletion events must be retained 12 months; request-level debug traces must be deletable/obfuscatable on request.

What Redwood can do today (initial position):
- Logical deletion: we can mark and remove records from the active datastore within 24 hours of validated request.
- Embeddings & caches: we actively scrub KV cache and generation traces on request; embeddings stored in vector stores are covered by the same logical deletion path.
- Backups: primary system snapshots are on a schedule; cold/archival backups may have longer retention windows due to provider snapshot chains (see questions below). This is the main constraint for "complete purge" semantics.

Open questions we need to confirm (next actions):
1) Can BrightFin accept a two-stage attestation: (a) confirmation that data is no longer accessible in primary/active stores within 24 hours, and (b) confirmation that backups have been purged according to backup-retention-specific timeline (see options below)?
2) Which regions are in-scope for strict 30-day backup purge (we currently saw EU + US regulatory needs; APAC optional)?
3) Is a signed attestation sufficient, or do you need a notarized/DocuSign-style confirmation for each RTBF event?

Proposed pragmatic options for BrightFin to choose from:
A) Standard: Logical deletion within 24 hours; initiate backup purge workflow; target full removal from accessible backups in 45 days (may be up to 60–90 days for cold-archive in some regions).
B) Accelerated (paid): Dedicated off-cycle backup sweep and targeted re-build to attempt purge within 14–30 days (depends on provider and encryption key rotation).
C) Private deployment: Redwood Private (VPC) or on-prem option allows tighter control over backup lifecycles and can meet 30-day purge SLAs in most cases.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Redwood to provide written playbook + SOC2 snapshot for our deletion process and backup constraints (I attached a first draft playbook). [Attachment: BrightFin-RTBF-playbook-v1.pdf]
- Redwood infra (Rishi) to analyze your backup config and confirm realistic purge timelines by region (ETA: May 13 infra call).
- Confirm whether BrightFin needs DocuSign attestation or a support-ticket confirmation flow.

If that matches your notes, we’ll schedule the infra deep-dive on Wed 13 May (I’ll send a calendar invite). Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Rishi/Monica and come back with the confirmed timeline after the infra review.

Best,

Subject: Re: Data deletion workflow & backup constraints — follow-up from discovery call

Thanks Ava — clear summary and helpful options. A few clarifications from our side:

- Regulatory constraint: our compliance team needs an assurance that no customer personal data will be restorable from backups beyond 30 days for EU subjects. US data can be 60 days. (We can share the specific policy excerpt.)
- Scope question: does the deletion include embeddings, completions logs, and inference traces tied to user IDs? We need these explicitly covered.
- Evidence: we prefer a signed attestation per purge (DocuSign OK). If Redwood can provide a one-off attestation for this account along with a standard SOC2/compliance summary that would speed our procurement.

One more ask: can you confirm whether backup snapshots use provider-managed immutable storage? Immutable snapshots would make an immediate "irreversible purge" impossible until retention expires — in that case we need an alternative mitigation (e.g., KMS key rotation to render data unreadable).

We’ll plan to join the infra call on Wed — add our infra lead (Irv Patel) if possible. Thanks — Lena

Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Security, BrightFin Inc.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 14:40:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Data deletion workflow & backup constraints — quick infra/legal note

Ava / Monica — forwarding with infra/legal context below (see Lena’s ask quoted). Short answers from infra:

On Sun, 11 May 2026 at 09:05 AM Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@brightfin.com> wrote:
> Regulatory constraint: our compliance team needs an assurance that no customer personal data will be restorable from backups beyond 30 days for EU subjects. US data can be 60 days.
> 
> Scope question: does the deletion include embeddings, completions logs, and inference traces tied to user IDs?

Infra/legal quick notes:
- Active store purge: confirmed — we have automation to remove records and associated vector-store entries within 24 hours of a validated RTBF event. That includes embeddings and linked cache entries.
- Backups: depends on the backup chain. Provider snapshot chains and incremental deltas can leave residual data in older snapshots. Typical timelines: short-term snapshots (hot backups) often purged within 30–45 days; cold/archival copies can be 60–90 days.
- Mitigation options:
  1) KMS key rotation: re-encrypting or rotating keys can effectively make archived snapshots unreadable — but note: we need customer sign-off for key rotations that impact recovery semantics.
  2) Targeted restore-and-scrub: spin up a temporary restore, scrub data, and re-snapshot; this is operationally heavy but can accelerate scrub to ~14–30 days depending on dataset size.

Recommendation to sales/legal for this deal: offer a two-part attestation: 24-hour removal from active stores (guaranteed) + backup purge target window (default 45 days). Offer an accelerated purge option as an add-on in the contract (documented cost/time estimates). If BrightFin requires a strict 30-day absolute backup purge in all regions, we should propose Redwood Private or a dedicated run for that SLA.

I’ve attached a short SOC2 summary we can share with BrightFin to unblock procurement.

- Rishi

Subject: Re: Data deletion workflow & backup constraints — follow-up and proposed timeline

Thanks Lena — appreciate the clarity. Based on Rishi’s infra notes, here’s a concrete proposal that I hope is acceptable and we can capture in the MA or SOW:

Agreed baseline (included in standard contract):
- Logical deletion: Redwood will remove personal data and associated embeddings/caches from the active systems within 24 hours of a validated RTBF request.
- Attestation: Redwood will provide a signed attestation confirming the 24-hour active-store deletion for each operational RTBF event.
- Backup purge target: Redwood will initiate a backup purge workflow targeting full non-restorability within 45 days for most regions; some cold-archive regions may extend to 60 days.

Optional accelerated path (add-on):
- Dedicated purge run (target 14–30 days) using targeted restore-and-scrub or key-rotation where feasible. We will produce a cost estimate if you want to move forward.

Next steps / action items:
1) Infra deep-dive: Wed, 13 May — Redwood infra (Rishi) + BrightFin infra (Irv) to review backup topology and confirm region-by-region timelines.
2) Procurement: Redwood to send SOC2 summary + the RTBF playbook we discussed. [Attachments: BrightFin-RTBF-playbook-v1.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf]
3) Contract language: Monica to draft the attestation clause and optional purge SOW for review (Monica, can you share a draft by EOD Thu?).

If BrightFin can confirm that a signed attestation (DocuSign) + the 45-day target is an acceptable baseline, we’ll proceed and include the accelerated option in the SOW. If you need absolute 30-day backing in all regions, we’ll outline Redwood Private / dedicated-run pricing separately.

I’ll send calendar invites for the May 13 deep-dive.

Best,
Ava Chen
Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
